about: The strong powers of lzrprf: each with the subs that hold it, its condition marks, why the browser needs it, the one act of the person that sets it off, and the selftest runs that show it does not happen without that act. CAPABILITIES.md says the same in sentences. Subs are named, never line numbers: perl tools/sub-map prints the lines. selftest checks that every system program lzrprf starts is in the list programs with the sub that starts it, and that every one listed there is still started.

powers.name: The application's tool: reading processes and launchd jobs, switching off a job, ending a process
powers.why: The tool shows what runs on this Mac (processes, launchd jobs of the account, who signed their programs) and lets the person switch off a launchd job of their own account or ask a process of their own to end.
powers.user_act: Look: the person opens the tool from the window (its icon in the bottom bar). Change: the person ticks a row in the tool and then confirms. A job the person switched off is kept in ~/.lzrprf/quieted and switched off again at each start and every 300 seconds while a window is open (sub tool_watch); that repeats the earlier tick and confirm, and the person switches it on again in the tool.
never: a job or process of the system or of Apple
changes: launchctl disable, then launchctl bootout (sub tool_off)
launchctl enable, then launchctl bootstrap (sub tool_wake)
signal TERM to a process of the person's own (sub tool_stop)
powers.selftest_note: The runs use stand-ins for what ps, launchctl, plutil and codesign say, so no real job or process is touched. Run tool: only a ticked and confirmed row is changed, and only a process of the person's own outside the system or a job of the account that is not Apple's can be ticked. Run toolbad: an answer of the application with one line out of form shows nothing and changes nothing. Run toolall: Show all processes lists every process with its use of a processor and memory (ps), its group, what it is (the application's word, else the manual page of its program read from this Mac's own man folders) and the note the person wrote, kept in ~/.lzrprf/procnotes after its log line; nothing of it is sent anywhere and nothing is changed.

powers.name: Fetching and running the installer of a newer release, outside every container
powers.why: An update replaces the application and lzrprf itself. The installer must write into the person's Applications and ~/.lzrprf, which no container allows, so it runs outside every container.
powers.user_act: Two acts. First a yes to looking for newer releases (kept with its address in ~/.lzrprf/look), or Check for updates in the cogwheel's menu for one look. Then Install it, for the newer release the window offers. The installer is run only after Install it. Restart after a finished install is a third press, and only then is /usr/bin/open used.
conditions: the release file names the installer place, and the second place when there is one, as https addresses (sub release_signed)
release.manifest, release.manifest.sig and release.manifest.approval are fetched beside each installer place, and the two places hold the same bytes
the approval holds for an approval key lzrprf carries (@APPROVAL_KEYS), namespace lzrbrwsr-approval, checked first
the release signature holds for the release key lzrprf carries ($RELEASE_KEY), namespace lzrbrwsr-release
both checked by /usr/bin/ssh-keygen in the verifier container ($VERIFIER)

the manifest is in its one form (sub manifest_read), of the published release number, newer than the installed one, signed no later than one day from now, not expired, valid at most 400 days, and names install.sh
the installer is fetched from both places, up to 12 tries 30 seconds apart, and the copies must be byte for byte the same
the installer's SHA-256 equals the manifest's install.sh line (sub installed)
it runs as /usr/bin/env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin HOME=... TERM=dumb /bin/sh install.sh auto, ended after 1800 seconds (sub install_run)
powers.known_state: @APPROVAL_KEYS is empty in lzrprf today, so every release is refused by lzrprf until an approval key is written there.
powers.selftest_note: Runs upno, uplater, upbad, upmoved, uplost and upunlogged show that without a kept yes, or after Later, nothing is fetched or installed. updiffer and upnosame show that differing places, or no place for the signed manifest, stop the update. upyes fetches the installer after the yes and, in a try, does not run it.
other_tests: the maker's own package test, not published here: the installer refuses a release without its signature or its approval, with a stranger's approval key, an approval of other bytes, either signature in the other's place, no approval key carried, two places that differ, an expired manifest, and a changed manifest

powers.name: The Tor client
programs: arti (beside the program, named by its SHA-256 in the release file)
powers.why: To fetch through Tor, with each site's host as the SOCKS user so each site has its own circuit.
powers.user_act: The person turns Tor on from its icon in the window's bottom bar (the window's line "tor on"). Tor off ends the client.
powers.selftest_note: A stand-in client relays SOCKS5. Run tor: the client starts on request, every request goes through it, Tor off ends it; the container is tried with /bin/cat. Run torfail: when Tor does not connect nothing is fetched, through Tor or directly, and the client is ended.

powers.name: The bookmark reader: reading other browsers' bookmark files
powers.why: To import bookmarks from Chrome, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, Firefox and Safari without lzrprf itself or the closed application reading the person's home folder.
powers.user_act: Opening the import wizard has the reader look whether each browser's folder is there. The person choosing a browser in the wizard has it read that browser's bookmark files. Allow on a folder in the Open panel has it try once more where macOS kept it out.
powers.selftest_note: Run importreader: on a fake home folder the reader reads the bookmark files and is refused History, Login Data, places.sqlite, History.db, the list of a profile folder and a file outside the home folder. Runs importkept and importallow: a panel answer nobody asked for, or Allow on another folder, is refused.

powers.name: The system's picture decoder (sips)
powers.why: The application cannot decode AVIF, HEIC or HEIF. The system's sips decodes such a picture into a PNG of at most 1024 pixels a side.
powers.user_act: A visit to a page (by any road of C4) whose picture the application hands back whole as AVIF, HEIC or HEIF. At every start sub holds also runs sips once in that container as one of the C2 tries.
powers.selftest_note: Run pictureslarge: a file the application changed by one byte is not given to the system. Run lostdecoder: a copy whose decoder container may read every file and reach the network is caught by the start tries, and nothing starts.

powers.name: The system's stream converter (avconvert)
powers.why: The window's player cannot read the sound of an MPEG-TS stream in its container. avconvert copies the stream's pictures and sound into an MP4 without decoding them (PresetPassthrough).
powers.user_act: A click on a video's place in the window, for an HLS stream that lzrprf joined as MPEG-TS with sound.
powers.selftest_note: Run videoplay: a video never clicked is never asked for. Run hlsmore: a stream with sound comes to the window as an MP4, and no folder of the converter is left. The converter container is tried from inside: the network and a file beside the stream are refused.

powers.name: The sound process (core-lzrbrwsr-sound): the system's osascript playing the sound of a page kept running
powers.why: macOS plays no sound in a process that cannot reach its register of sound components (com.apple.audio.AudioComponentRegistrar), and the window's container keeps that name out by the owner's choice. The sound process is the one place that may reach it, with the sound server and the CoreServices daemon osascript needs, and nothing else.
powers.user_act: A click or a key handed to a page kept running, within $SOUND_PRESS_SECONDS of which the page plays a sound (C12): the process is started for the first such sound of a window, and ended once nothing has played for $SOUND_IDLE seconds, or with the window. Or your click on a video's Sound off (C22): its MP4 is handed over and its sound follows the window's clock of the picture; a video whose sound stays off starts none.
powers.selftest_note: Run soundplays: lzrprf's own sub sounding and text, at no volume on samples of silence, play each sound and answer each play with what the system's players said. Run soundwindow: the same text in the window's container plays nothing and says so. Run soundvideo: an MP4 of silence with a sound track, handed over in lzrprf's lines, plays at no volume within 40 ms of the picture's clock. Run soundvideowindow: the window's container plays no video's sound. Run livesound: a sound a page starts with no press before it is passed on to nothing.

powers.name: The terminal (LZRTRMNL): the person's login shell
programs: the person's login shell, as /etc/shells lists it
core-lzrbrwsr-trmnl (beside the program, named by its SHA-256 in the release file)
powers.container: the shell: none, it runs as the person; its drawing: $TRMNL_CONTAINER with $TRMNL_LIMITS
powers.why: A terminal is a tab of the browser. A shell has the person's rights by what it is; what is kept in a container is the program that reads everything the shell and its programs write and turns it into the laid lines of the tab.
powers.user_act: A press of the terminal icon on the local home of a window that is neither incognito nor Tor. After that, only the person's keys and paste reach the shell. The window reads the clipboard only on the person's paste and writes it only on the person's copy, with the selected text; a program's OSC 52 is passed over.
powers.selftest_note: No selftest run yet. Measured headless on macOS 27.2 (managed-projects/lzrbrwsr/architecture/lzrtrmnl.md): the drawing container holds only its two pipes and /dev/null, and an answer to a question the shell never asked is not written.

programs.act: The start of the file: lzrprf started by another perl starts itself again with the system's own. find: a lookup of a host after the request's line is in the log (C5). proven: runs selftest after the person's yes to testing (C11). incognito_opened, pulled_command, profile_command, tor_window_opened: a new lzrprf window after New Incognito Window, a tab pulled out, a profile opened, or Tor asked for in a window that is not a Tor window (C17). The others start a contained program; decoding and converting are handed it by system_decoded, system_converted, holds and decoder_named. limited: only when lzrprf itself holds more memory than a container may, a perl that sets that one limit and becomes sandbox-exec ($ROOM_SET).
Every contained start: the page, fetch, window, decoder, converter, sound, reader, verifier, Tor and terminal containers.

run: the window itself, in $WINDOW_CONTAINER, at each start of a window (C10). sounding: the sound process, in $SOUND_CONTAINER, for the first sound of a page kept running in a window (C12). witnessed starts the process that asks the system whether a process is contained ($WITNESS, asked by sub inside); decoder_named asks it for the decoder ($NAMED) (C3).
Each request, in $FETCH, over the one connection lzrprf made (C3, C6, C7); the roads to a request are listed in C4.
Checks a release's two signatures in $VERIFIER (signature_checked, asked by signature_holds) after the person said yes to looking for releases (C25).

tool_look, tool_stop and tool_procs: the tool (C20). shell_held: one shell reads its own memory size (ps -o vsz= -p $$) once as a window begins (shell_measured), and every container is limited to that and 2 GiB more (sub limited); without that number, the first container to start measures it. The sound and terminal shells read their own before they set their limits.
Reads a launchd property list for the tool (C20).
Reads who signed a program, for the tool (C20). Read only (codesign -dv).
route -n get, read only, as route_asked writes it and route and find run it: whether an address of a looked-up host leads into the person's own network (C8). Asked for each request's addresses.

install_run: runs the installer with an empty environment after Install it (C25). The limits: the sound and terminal shells, their limits set, become env -i with an empty environment but for lzrprf's own names, and env starts sandbox-exec with the contained program.
Sets the limits (ulimit) of the sound and terminal containers, and redirections, before a program starts; measures the memory a shell holds once (shell_held); and runs the installer after Install it.
open -n on the application, after a finished install and the person's press on restart.
Marks a kept log (log, log.new) to be left out of Time Machine backups; only when the person chose to keep a log.
Reads kern.osversion, the build of macOS, for the selftest mark (C11). Read only.
Never started on purpose: the C2 tries ask a container to start it, and the container must refuse.
